canonicalExplanation.summary: Boxes have **intrinsic** sizes from their content: `min-content` (as narrow as possible — the longest unbreakable word), `max-content` (no wrapping at all). Flex and grid items by default refuse to shrink below their **min-content**, so one long URL or code line can force a whole layout wider. Fixes: `minmax(0, 1fr)` in grid, `min-width: 0` on flex items, and letting text wrap with `overflow-wrap: anywhere`.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A two-column layout looks perfect — until a comment contains a 120-character URL. The main column refuses to shrink, pushes the sidebar off-screen, and the page scrolls sideways on phones. A grid track uses minmax(0,1fr) so long content may shrink instead of forcing the entire layout wider. In this lesson you'll implement a component that grows, shrinks and wraps without clipping realistic content.

```predict
{"question": "`grid-template-columns: 1fr 250px`. A cell in the 1fr column contains a very long unbroken URL. What happens?", "options": ["The 1fr column shrinks and the URL wraps", "The column grows to fit the URL, widening the grid"], "answer": 1, "why": "A plain `1fr` track has an automatic minimum of its content's min-content size. `minmax(0, 1fr)` removes that minimum."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Rules, declarations and values** and **Lengths, percentages and viewport units**.

sections.heading: The model: content sets a minimum unless you lift it
sections.body:
```css
.layout {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) 250px;   /* can shrink below content */
  gap: 1rem;
}
.comment { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }            /* long URLs may break */

.row { display: flex; gap: 1rem; }
.row > .main { flex: 1; min-width: 0; }         /* flex item may shrink */
```

| Keyword / rule | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `min-content`. | narrowest without overflow (longest word). |
| `max-content`. | widest, no wrapping. |
| `fit-content`. | max-content but capped by available space. |
| `1fr` (grid). | share of space, but min = auto (content). |
| `minmax(0, 1fr)`. | share of space, allowed to shrink to 0. |
| `min-width: 0` (flex). | lets the item shrink below content size. |

```reveal
{"prompt": "Once the column can shrink, what stops the URL overflowing?", "answer": "The text must be allowed to break: `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (or `break-word`). Otherwise it just sticks out of the narrower box."}
```

examples.title: The long URL that widened the layout
examples.situation: A grid track uses minmax(0,1fr) so long content may shrink instead of forcing the entire layout wider.
walkthrough: **Problem:** `grid-template-columns: 1fr 250px` — a 120-character URL sets the 1fr track's minimum, so the grid overflows the phone screen.
**Fix the track:** `minmax(0, 1fr)` lets the main column shrink below its content size.
**Let text wrap:** `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on comments; the browser will render the URL across lines, and the sidebar stays in view.
examples.result: The layout fits at 320px wide, and the long URL wraps instead of widening everything.

examples.title: The flex title that wouldn't truncate
examples.situation: A card row has an icon and a title (`flex: 1`) with `text-overflow: ellipsis`, but the long title pushes the icon out instead of truncating.
walkthrough: Flex items default to `min-width: auto`, i.e. their content's min-content size.
The title can't shrink, so ellipsis never kicks in.
Fix: `min-width: 0` on the title, plus `overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis`.
examples.result: The title truncates with an ellipsis and the icon stays visible.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: A 1fr track always shrinks below its content's minimum without any additional rule.
misconceptions.correction: A 1fr track has an automatic minimum equal to its content's min-content size, so long unbreakable content widens it. Use minmax(0, 1fr) (or min-width: 0 for flex items) and allow text to wrap.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The long URL that widened the layout", what set the column's minimum?

analogy.example: Intrinsic sizing is like **packing a suitcase with a rigid item**: soft clothes (wrappable text) squeeze, but a long umbrella (an unbreakable URL) sets the suitcase's minimum length — unless you allow it to fold (overflow-wrap) and the suitcase to be smaller than the umbrella (minmax(0,1fr)).
usefulFor: lifting the minimum and allowing wraps
limitations: Umbrellas don't fold at arbitrary points; text can with overflow-wrap.
Suitcases have fixed sizes; grid tracks share space.

remediation.explanation: When something overflows, select it in DevTools and check: **Is it a flex/grid item with an automatic minimum? Can its text wrap?** Fix the minimum first, then the wrapping.

recap.summary: To implement a component that grows, shrinks and wraps without clipping realistic content, remember flex and grid items default to a min-content minimum; lift it with minmax(0, 1fr) or min-width: 0, allow wrapping with flex-wrap and overflow-wrap, and stress-test with long content.
